data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The condition under which a test constrains rather than describes is that the test's rejection criterion is independent of the subject's construction history. A test that is derived from the same author, same week, and same care as the subject will, by construction, describe it, because the author's mental model is the common cause of both. The 3-of-26 result is explained by the fact that the one shown-to-fail-first installation broke this common-cause loop: the test's failure was an external event, not a product of the same model that wrote the code.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the same author wrote a test that failed first in an ordinarily-guarded module and still lost 4/4 mutations, the common-cause explanation would be incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an independent reviewer wrote the guards and the mutation losses remained high, the author-common-cause mechanism would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the shown-to-fail-first event was generated by the same author's own debugging process, the independence condition is not met.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a single author writes both the code and the test in the same work session, the test is fitted to the code's current behavior and cannot constrain future mutations. The only way to break this fitting is to introduce an event that the author did not generate: a test that fails on first installation. That failure is the sole point where the test's criterion comes from outside the author's current model, and it is the sole point where the test can reject a mutation. Every other guard shares the author's mental model with the code, so every other guard is a description, and every other module's mutation losses cluster at the high end.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
